items.text: In two weeks this room stops meeting — the next two Wednesdays are sendings, not endings. On the other side: a summer with no Wednesday in it.
Somewhere out there — this summer, or in twenty years — every person in this room will hit a season where the practices go gray
The most dangerous thing on the long walk is not the dryness — it is the wrong diagnosis of the dryness
So tonight we hand you the equipment for that season — on purpose, at the threshold, before anyone needs it
Psalm 23:4 — “Even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for you are with me.” The road goes through.
Now the teaching — in the seniors’ voices, not ours

panel.label: ISAIAH 50:10
lines: “Who among you fears the LORD and obeys the voice of his servant? Let him who walks in darkness and has no light trust in the name of the LORD and rely on his God.”

slides.title: The Signs Card — the Four Kinds of Dry

items.text: The danger is not the dryness — it is the wrong diagnosis. One question sorts everything: “Which way does the desire point?”
Neglect — the desire has faded and the distance doesn’t ache; the world tastes fine. First step: wake and turn — rebuild the rhythm
Worn out — the desire is buried under duty; you want escape, not God. First step: rest — a lighter yoke, smaller faithful steps, stay put
The enemy’s dry wind — accused, pressured, a voice counseling change: quit, undo, leave. First step: resist — change nothing, pray a little more, tell someone
God’s own stripping — the desire intact and starving; the ache is the sign. First step: receive — wait, stay faithful, stay accompanied
Three and four command opposite motions — one says fight, the other says yield. When you cannot tell which you are in, do not decide alone — that is what Companions are for.
Four rules on the card — your own heart only; in every case, tell someone; no big decisions in the dark; know when to call the doctor

panel.label: THE SENTENCE TO CARRY HOME
lines: “The fact that His absence hurts you is the evidence that He has not gone. Drifting hearts do not ache. Abandoned fields do not thirst. A dry season is not a verdict.”

slides.title: The Path Home Card — the Written Door

items.text: For the one who leaves and concludes a room like this would not want them back — most churches leave the way back unwritten. Not here.
Come as you are — conviction is specific and hopeful and draws you toward home; shame is vague and hopeless and drives you away
Tell it straight — to God in plain words, and to one trusted person; you choose the person and how much
Grieve what needs grieving — lament is faith with tears in its voice
Return to the table — small; do not start over, begin again on the next available day
Let it be celebrated — in the Lord’s own story of return, the ending is not a probation meeting. It is a feast.
The witnessed filing — everyone files the card now, while we watch each other do it: “The door is not locked. The light is on.”

panel.label: LUKE 15:20
lines: “But while he was still a long way off, his father saw him and felt compassion, and ran and embraced him and kissed him.”
The father was watching the road. He ran first, embraced first, and asked for no accounting before the robe.

items.text: Take out your journal — the one you have been writing in since September. If yours is missing, take paper and walk the year from memory.
Go back to the beginning and read forward — you’re walking the road again, not re-taking the class
Where did I begin?
Where did He meet me? — mark those pages; fold a corner
What do I not want to lose?
Twelve minutes, in quiet — parents and teens both. Then find your one sentence.

slides.title: One Sentence, and the Testimony Gathering

items.text: One sentence each — where He met you this year, or what you don’t want to lose. Just the sentence; no story around it. A parent starts.
Pass-anytime holds — a pass gets the same nod a sentence gets
Then one more invitation, genuinely optional: your sentence, read aloud at the sendings — Week 21 or Week 22
Written down exactly as you say it, read back for your nod — signed or anonymous, your choice
“An empty card is a complete answer.” Nothing written, nothing noted, and nobody will ask again.
H20.1 — the bookend to orientation’s Pre-Series Survey. Home tonight; back in the bin at the Week 21 door.
This is a pilot — the first year this has ever run, anywhere. Your honest answers — especially the critical ones — are a gift to families you will never meet.
The same covenant covers it: no scores, no grades, mirrors not levers
One per person — parents and teens each do their own. About twenty minutes. Signed or anonymous, your choice.
